title: I Can't Afford Not to Care Anymore
subtitle: In Which Waluigi Opens A Door, Says Something Magnificent, And Is Immediately Presented With The Bill
filed: 5 Aethel, 1040 BF — filed from the desk, in handcuffs Waluigi has already escaped from
pullQuote: Waluigi opened the door. Waluigi said the line. Waluigi had FOUR SECONDS to enjoy it. WAH.
standfirst: The sequel to the doorway, narrated by the man who opened it and has not stopped paying for it. A treant nobody could read, a bomb thrown badly, a guard whose nine words break the whole case, four special forces operatives who identified a dwarf by his ONESIE, and a lady of the manor who answered to the word carnivorous. Waluigi was in this one. Waluigi is in handcuffs. Waluigi has notes.

sections.heading: Waluigi Said The Sentence And Then Waluigi Had To PAY For The Sentence
sections.body:
Last filing ended with Waluigi opening a door. Waluigi wants that established FIRST, in Waluigi's own words, in an archive Waluigi controls, because in about ninety seconds Waluigi is going to be dragged down a corridor by a dwarf and Waluigi needs the reader to remember whose fault that was.

It was Waluigi's fault. There. FILED.

Here is the sequence, and Waluigi is going to run it slowly because the whole session lives inside it. Hjumpik said *we can't fight every battle*. Waluigi said *then if they're that weak, we should take them on*. Hjumpik's hand came up. Waluigi reached PAST the hand. The door opened. And Hjumpik — a dwarf who has been doing arithmetic at Waluigi for three sessions — asked the only question that mattered: *since when did you care?*

And Waluigi heard Waluigi's own mouth say: **"I can't afford not to care anymore."**

Beautiful. Devastating. Genuinely one of the finest lines this archive has ever produced, and Waluigi produced it live, unrehearsed, in a corridor, over the sound of something enormous. Waluigi has been writing for TEN YEARS and forty volumes to arrive at a sentence that good.

Waluigi had approximately FOUR SECONDS to enjoy it.

Because the room on the other side of that door contained the Revel, and the Revel was not alone, and the thing standing in the middle of the floor was a treant with its FULL HEIGHT under it. Not the half-dead shrub Waluigi had been waving around as a rhetorical device for the previous twenty minutes of hallway. Not the mound the goblins had already stabbed most of the life out of. A treant. Upright. Unbothered. With the floor taking its weight the way a floor takes something that intends to stay.

It TURNED.

Waluigi would like to describe what Waluigi did next as *holding the line* and will be describing it that way in every retelling for the rest of Waluigi's career. What Waluigi actually did was stand in a doorway with Waluigi's arms out while a dwarf attached himself to Waluigi's sleeve.

And behind Waluigi, Toad Lee had the axe out and was looking at the thing with an expression nobody has ever successfully read, which is NORMAL for Toad Lee and Waluigi has stopped filing it as notable.

But here is the part of this section that Waluigi needs the reader to actually absorb, because it is going to matter for the next ten thousand words: the fey in that room were not all fighting the tree. Some of them were fighting FOR it. The Revel has been a party for three sessions — a party, an actual party, with drinking and theatre and a lost dog — and it has now produced combatants on BOTH SIDES of the same floor, and not one being in this manor can tell you which fey is which until it SWINGS at someone.

Waluigi opened a door on a civil war and called it a monster. WAH.

sections.heading: The Dwarf Could Not Read The Tree, So The Dwarf Read WALUIGI Instead
sections.body:
Hjumpik looked at the treant for what Waluigi will GENEROUSLY call three seconds and then delivered a tactical assessment of such crushing dismissiveness that Waluigi is still annoyed about it: this did not look really good, and was kind of pointless.

POINTLESS. Waluigi opens a door on the largest creature in the building and the dwarf calls it POINTLESS, like a man returning soup.

Except — and Waluigi hates this part, Waluigi wants the reader to understand the personal cost of what Waluigi is about to write — the dwarf was RIGHT, and he was right for a reason Waluigi had not thought about once.

**He could not tell how damaged it was.**

Think about that. Actually think about it, because Waluigi did not, and Waluigi is the one who FILES things. Bark does not bleed anywhere a person can see it. A treant with forty hit points left and a treant with a hundred and forty look EXACTLY THE SAME from a doorway. There is no wound. There is no stagger. There is no red on the floor. There is a tree, and the tree is either nearly dead or entirely fine, and nothing about its surface will tell you which.

Now go back to the library. Waluigi's ENTIRE argument — the one Waluigi built a whole corridor row on top of — was that these plants are weak. And the evidence for that argument was a shambling mound that was VISIBLY half-eaten, chewed on by the fey residents before the party ever got there, so mangled that a goblin staff finished it. Waluigi looked at a creature whose damage was written on the outside of it and drew a conclusion about an entire species.

Hjumpik looked at a creature whose damage was not written anywhere and refused to draw one.

That is the whole difference between them and Waluigi is putting it in writing ONCE and then never mentioning it again.

So the dwarf stopped assessing and started moving, which is what Hjumpik does when the numbers stop being available. He announced, to nobody, to the room, to the general air: "I'm going to drag Waluigi out of this."

And then he did.

Waluigi would like the archive to record, with precision, that Waluigi was not CARRIED. Waluigi was PULLED. There is an enormous difference between those two verbs and it is the only dignity available to Waluigi anywhere in this section, and Waluigi intends to hold onto it with both hands, which is more than Waluigi managed with the doorframe.

The dwarf is wrong about one thing, though, and Waluigi will die on this. He said the fight was POINTLESS. It was not pointless. It was UNKNOWN. Those are completely different words, and every single argument in this session lives in the gap between them.

sections.heading: The Fey Had A PLAN, And The Dwarf Walked Straight Through The Middle Of It
sections.body:
The Revel's spirits noticed the party leaving and objected IMMEDIATELY and at VOLUME, which Waluigi respects as a performance choice.

*Wait — our plan, the ambush — where are you going?*

Two sessions. TWO SESSIONS these people have been building an ambush. There has been planning. There has been a war room. There has been a table-sized tactical map with barrel tallies in the margin. And the dwarf they staked it on turned around in the doorway and said the single most deflating sentence available to him:

**"It's not an ambush if it's right here. So... unless you know how strong this guy is, I won't fight them."**

*Ugh,* said the Revel. That is the actual recorded response. A faction of immortal fey, generations of courtly scheming behind them, and their entire counter-argument was *ugh*.

Waluigi wants this line carved into something. It is the first time in this whole arc that somebody has said the quiet mechanical truth OUT LOUD. An ambush is a fight you CHOSE. A fight in a doorway you happened to open is a fight the ROOM chose. Hjumpik will take the first one all day and twice on rest days. He will not take the second one at ANY price, and the fey — who invented the plan, who have been living inside the plan — could not process the distinction fast enough to argue with it.

Meanwhile Waluigi was still being towed down a hallway like disputed cargo.

"Why are you pulling me away from the action?"

"Well, there's a giant tree you ran into the room with. I'm trying to save your life. *Strategy.*"

STRATEGY. He said the word with the emphasis ON it. He used it like a hammer. He has been using it like a hammer since the first hallway and Waluigi has never once enjoyed it.

And the horrible thing — the thing Waluigi is filing here and then immediately going to contradict in the very next section — is that the man had just described the situation with total accuracy. Waluigi DID run into a room with a giant tree in it. Waluigi did it on purpose. Waluigi did it while making a speech. The dwarf's summary of events is unimprovable and Waluigi has read it four times looking for a crack.

Waluigi could not find one, so Waluigi started shouting about GLORY instead, which the reader should understand is Waluigi's recognised procedure when the facts stop cooperating. WAH.

sections.heading: The Hallway Row, Round Two: Waluigi Said The Unforgivable Thing And Meant It
sections.body:
"Bah. I hear you." Waluigi DID hear him. Hearing him has never once stopped Waluigi and it did not start here. "But think of it — the *glory*. Think about the manor. We have been running away for so long. What's the point? This manor will collapse."

And Hjumpik said four words like a door closing: **"You pick your fights."**

That is his entire philosophy. Four words. He has been carrying it around this house for three sessions like a man carrying a plate through a crowd.

So Waluigi broke it over him.

"You pick your fights? Then why are we in this mess?" Waluigi did not lower Waluigi's voice and Waluigi is not going to pretend otherwise in Waluigi's own archive. "Because you let someone get away. Because you took inaction. That guy ran away — and you HEALED him into a giant plant. I'm tired of running. Toad Lee follows you like a giant stub."

Waluigi said that. About Toad Lee. Who was STANDING THERE.

The reader should sit with that for a moment, because Waluigi has, and Waluigi is going to come back to it later in this cut and it is not going to be comfortable when Waluigi does.

And Hjumpik — who had a fistful of Waluigi's sleeve, who had just hauled Waluigi out of a room, who had every right to squeeze — let go.

Not dramatically. There was no speech. He just OPENED HIS HAND, and Waluigi's sleeve came back, and the two of them stood in a hallway in a house that is being eaten alive, having finally said the true things at each other instead of around each other.

"What should we do, then?" he said. "Since you love fighting — I'll follow what you say, and see if you're right."

And Waluigi — who has spent three sessions complaining about this dwarf's leadership, who has filed FORMAL OBJECTIONS to this dwarf's marching orders, who once put a written note in a margin about it — handed it straight back.

"I have been leading you guys. What do you think, Mr Bossman?"

MR BOSSMAN. Waluigi said MR BOSSMAN. In a corridor. To a man who had just offered Waluigi command of the party.

Here is the honest note, and Waluigi is putting it in the front half rather than the back because it will not survive being saved: neither of them wanted it. Waluigi did not want the party and Hjumpik did not want to keep it, and the two of them stood there passing a leadership dispute back and forth like a hot dish nobody wanted to set down on good furniture.

The archive files it as a command crisis resolved by MUTUAL REFUSAL, which is not in any manual Waluigi has ever read, and which — Waluigi will admit this once — worked.

sections.heading: Waluigi Asked For THEATRE And The Universe Delivered It With Interest
sections.body:
Hjumpik pointed at Toad Lee and put a bomb in his hand.

Not *gave*. POINTED first, and then PLACED. Waluigi is being precise about the choreography because the choreography is the joke. The Toad looked at the bomb. The bomb, one of Wario's Bob-ombs, looked at nobody, because bombs do not have that facility.

"We need something theatrical," Waluigi said, because Waluigi DID need something theatrical and Waluigi maintains the assessment was correct. "Toad Lee — throw the bomb."

He threw the bomb.

He MISSED.

And the bomb was picked up — picked UP, by hand, deliberately — by the House Guard veteran, and from that exact moment the evening stopped having any recognisable shape at all. Waluigi has filed a lot of engagements. Waluigi has never filed one that went sideways from a single failed throw quite this efficiently.

A guard holding a live Bob-omb in a corridor packed with fey who cannot agree on which side they are on is not a tactical situation. It is a CATEGORY ERROR. And a room presented with a category error resolves it the way rooms always do, which is loudly and in every direction at once.

"You're a deserter!" somebody shouted at Hjumpik. "Deserters get KILLED."

"You didn't say you'd fight this battle — you're attacking ME? **Attack the TREE.**"

*Attack the tree.* Waluigi would like that framed. A dwarf standing in a burning argument, with a bomb loose in the room and a deserter charge against his name, pointing at the ACTUAL ENEMY and having to explain it to people who were already swinging.

Waluigi's own contribution to the tactical picture, filed verbatim and without defence: "Well, I guess it's, uh — there's a bomb in there, and people started going crazy. And now there's TWO. They're MULTIPLYING. That's not good."

*That's not good.* Waluigi is an archivist of ten years and forty volumes and that is the sentence Waluigi produced.

A guard, helpfully, from somewhere in the mess: *it's stronger than you three combined.*

And the treant animated a SECOND TREANT — cast it, as an action, casually, in the middle of a fight it was not even losing — while Waluigi stood there stone-faced watching a tree manufacture another tree in a room Waluigi had personally insisted the party enter.

Waluigi asked for theatre. Waluigi received THEATRE. The request and the catastrophe were separated by one bad throw from a Toad, and Waluigi has absolutely no standing to complain about either, and Waluigi is going to complain about both anyway, at length, in this archive, forever. WAH.

sections.heading: One Question. FOUR SECONDS. Nobody In This House Had Asked It All WEEK.
sections.body:
"Are these guys weak to fire damage?"

"They're wood, so probably."

That is it. That is the whole exchange. Four seconds, two lines, and Waluigi is filing it with the same weight this archive gives to a signed treaty, because on the evidence of this entire session it was the most PRODUCTIVE conversation the party has had since the kitchen.

Waluigi needs the reader to understand the scale of the failure it exposes.

**Nobody in this manor has tested the vegetation for the obvious weakness.** Not one being. Go down the list.

The household has been STABBING it. Three sessions of stabbing. The house guard has been shooting it with heavy crossbows at a hundred feet — the ledger has them doing it, over and over, into a treant, at range, like men trying to fell an oak with a hole punch. The Revel has been putting it to SLEEP, casting Sleep at a plant, repeatedly, which Waluigi assumes is some sort of fey cultural practice because it cannot possibly be a plan. Red has been POISONING it, which is the only thing in the building that works, and even she is doing it with soup.

And the party? The party has a caster in it. Waluigi has been throwing magic missiles and ice lances down hallways for three sessions like a man showing off at a fair.

A house has been under siege by WOOD for a WEEK, and the first person to say the word *fire* out loud said it in a corridor, WHILE RETREATING, as a passing thought, and nobody wrote it down except Waluigi.

Waluigi is going to be thinking about this section for a very long time, and Waluigi wants the record to show that NONE of the resulting thoughts are flattering to anybody present. Including — Waluigi will say it before someone else does — including Waluigi, who has been in this manor as long as any of them, who has a spell list, who has been complaining about the strategic competence of everyone around him in two consecutive filings, and who did not think of it either.

The question was asked. It was answered. It was CORRECT. And then everybody kept walking. WAH.

sections.heading: The Dwarf MANAGED Waluigi And Waluigi Noticed And Waluigi ALLOWED It
sections.body:
Hjumpik decided to go help the people upstairs, and he pitched it — actually PITCHED it, out loud, like a man selling a cart: "I'll do that. That's, ummm — win-win. I'll help you, and I'll take out more tree monsters."

Win-win. The dwarf discovered SALESMANSHIP in the middle of a corridor and it was the worst sales patter Waluigi has ever been subjected to.

"Let's go find the others. *Strategy*, right?"

Strategy again. THIRD time. He is doing it deliberately at this point, he knows exactly what it does to Waluigi, and Waluigi is documenting the abuse.

So Waluigi told him, plainly, that Waluigi likes theatre more than strategy. Which is TRUE. Waluigi has never once pretended otherwise. Waluigi is an archivist, and an archive with no theatre in it is a list.

And then Hjumpik said the single most competent thing Waluigi has witnessed in this entire campaign, and Waluigi is going to reproduce it in full because it deserves the space:

**"Put your own theatrics into it. So we don't die, and you get your theatrics."**

Read that again. That is not a man winning an argument. A man winning an argument would have said *stop wanting the spectacle*, and Waluigi would have dug in, and the two of them would still be in that corridor now, being eaten by scenery.

He did not say that. He said: route the spectacle THROUGH the survival. Keep the thing you want. Change where it comes out.

Waluigi has been MANAGED. Waluigi noticed AT THE TIME — Waluigi wants that in the record, Waluigi was not fooled, Waluigi saw the handle going in — and Waluigi allowed it, which Waluigi maintains is a fundamentally different transaction and Waluigi will not be taking questions.

"Okay. For now. I still want that thing dead. If you run away, I'll stay and fight."

And that is where the argument ended. Not in agreement. Nobody agreed. What the two of them reached in that corridor was an EXCHANGE RATE — so much survival bought with so much spectacle, payable on demand — and Waluigi has to admit that a rate of exchange between two people who want incompatible things is worth considerably more than a truce between two people pretending they want the same one.

sections.heading: NINE WORDS From A Man Nobody Has Relieved, And They Break The Entire File
sections.body:
The same reinforcements guard was standing in the hallway. He said he had been guarding the hallway. As far as this archive can establish, he has been guarding that hallway the ENTIRE TIME — through the library, through the kitchen, through the fungus, through everything — because nobody has ever come to tell him to stop.

"What happened to the reinforcements?"

"They died."

"From the plants?"

**"Not from plants. From other people. They had sword slashes."**

Waluigi wants a line drawn under that in a colour the reader cannot ignore, and then Waluigi wants the reader to understand that Waluigi has been prosecuting the WRONG CASE for three sessions.

The overgrowth does not carry swords. Waluigi has watched it work. The treants CLUB and they throw bark — the ledger has a Hail of Bark attack in it, twenty-two damage, ranged, piercing. The violet fungus ROTS. The shambling mound ENGULFS. Every single casualty this house has taken from vegetation has LOOKED like vegetation did it, because vegetation has exactly one vocabulary and it has been speaking it fluently in every room.

These did not look like that. Somebody with an EDGED WEAPON killed the manor's reinforcements in a corridor, while the entire household's attention was pointed at the trees, and the only being who noticed is a guard nobody has relieved, nobody has debriefed, and nobody has thanked.

And then he made it worse by being USEFUL. Told that Red's cooking withers the overgrowth on contact, he asked the obvious question that four adventurers had failed to ask in two full days: why not put the soup in a BOMB?

Hjumpik: "We need a bomb specialist."

Waluigi: "Oh. Wario is one."

And there the thread STOPS. That is where it ends. Waluigi has a poison supplier in the kitchen, a bomb specialist named out loud in the corridor, a delivery problem with an obvious solution, and NOBODY BUILT ANYTHING.

Here is Waluigi dropping the voice, because this is the beat where Waluigi has to be honest instead of loud. Waluigi has spent two filings being magnificent about this party's incompetence. Waluigi has called Hjumpik incompetent to his face in a hallway. And the single most important piece of intelligence in three sessions came from a man in a corridor who was not invited to ANY of the planning, who was not asked a leading question, and who gave the inconvenient answer instead of the easy one — and the party heard it, and walked past it, and Waluigi walked past it WITH them.

There is a second killer in this house. It uses a blade. Nobody has examined a single body. Waluigi has filed it as a lead, and if the next session does not pull that thread, Waluigi will pull it personally and be COMPLETELY insufferable about it. WAH.

sections.heading: A Closed Door, A Change Of Species, And The Most Casual Sentence Of The Night
sections.body:
Before all that — Waluigi should do this in order — there was the coin business, which Waluigi is filing in three sentences because that is roughly how long it took and because Waluigi has no idea what happened.

Hjumpik shook his coins. A shadow came up the hall and resolved, as it walked, into the purple thing from the bathroom — the violet fungus, the one in the TOILET, the one the party left in there because there was a more interesting door available. The satyr killed it.

That is the whole event. And the notable thing is NOT the fungus. The notable thing is that Hjumpik has a way of shaking a purse that BRINGS SOMETHING TO HIM, that what it brought was a competent swordsman who fights on the party's side, and that not one being at that table asked him a single question about it. Waluigi is filing an open question rather than a guess, and the reader should understand that costs Waluigi something, because Waluigi ENJOYS guessing.

Then the kitchen.

Red wanted the door closed. She needed to change; she had got her clothes dirty.

Hjumpik: "Why?"

"I need privacy."

"But you have cooks in there."

"We're all women here."

The door closed. Waluigi stood in a corridor. The door opened.

And Red was HUMAN. Not a red bugbear demon — a woman, in the same coat, standing in her own kitchen doorway with flour still on her hands.

Hjumpik: "Who are you?"

"No, no — it's *me*. The trees are multiplying."

Waluigi has read that exchange back four separate times looking for the seam and there ISN'T ONE. So here is the archive's position, filed plainly and without a joke on the end of it: the manor's kitchen commander changed SPECIES behind a closed door, offered no account of it whatsoever, and the first thing out of her mouth on the other side was a TACTICAL UPDATE.

She was not hiding. She was REPORTING.

"We need an actual solution," she said. "How did this happen?"

"From a guy with mushrooms growing on him."

"We need to take it out at the source."

Hjumpik: "I didn't want to kill an innocent."

Red: "Sometimes we have to kill for the greater good."

There is an ENTIRE political philosophy in that exchange — a whole argument about necessity and innocence that empires have come apart over — and the two of them had it in a kitchen doorway in about nine seconds and neither of them noticed they were having it. Waluigi noticed. Waluigi files these things. That is what Waluigi is FOR.

sections.heading: Four Operatives, Four Colours, And A ONESIE
sections.body:
Hjumpik tried a door. Locked. Red said there had been fighting behind it — slashing sounds, which the reader should now find considerably more interesting than it sounded at the time — and that she had opened it after the plants left, and then a hand—

He asked to check it. She agreed to unlock it.

Three guards stood there. And then the magical girl sequence started.

*I'm Red.* *And I'm Green.* *And I'm Yellow.* *And I'm Black* — and the fourth one TURNED INTO A SHADOW.

"Like a black person, or—"

Waluigi opened Waluigi's mouth and Waluigi CLOSED IT AGAIN, and the reader should understand that has happened perhaps four times in Waluigi's recorded life and Waluigi was proud of every one of them.

"Okay, so there are monsters over here. Have you fought any?"

"Yeah, we got the monsters. This goblin guy and demon guy." A satyr, for the record. Waluigi is correcting it in the margin because somebody has to.

"Who are you guys? You don't look like guards here."

"We're part of the Colour Division."

"Colour Division?"

"Special forces."

"For who?"

"The Iron Legionaries. We were sent here to look for a dwarf named **Hjumpoo**."

HJUMPOO. Four elite operatives crossed a planar boundary, into a house being eaten by carnivorous architecture, on a contract retrieval — and they got the NAME WRONG.

And Hjumpik — standing directly in front of them, being looked at, in a wolf-pelt onesie — said: "Hjumpik, you stupid."

He CORRECTED THEM. He corrected the people hunting him. On the pronunciation.

"Why?"

"He took longer than five nights. His time's up. They want him back for the mission."

"I can relay that information to him."

"Really?"

*Really?* They nearly took it. Waluigi watched three trained operatives lean toward *yes* because it would have been EASIER.

And then Black — who is the only one of the four who was doing any work — said it. "Hey — you ARE Hjumpik. You have the signature wolf-pelt onesie on."

And Hjumpik produced the finest legal defence in the history of this archive: "Uhh, you know, a lot of dwarves use this stuff. It's kinda racist. *All* dwarves use wolf pelt."

It did not work. He closed the door SLOWLY and ran upstairs.

Waluigi wants one thing on the record. Four special forces operatives crossed between PLANES to collect one man, and the identification was made on a GARMENT. Not a sigil. Not a writ. Not a description. The onesie. He has been wearing it in front of Waluigi for three sessions and Waluigi has never ONCE thought of it as EVIDENCE. WAH.

sections.heading: Three Months Became Five Months In The Middle Of His Own Sentence
sections.body:
The chase went up the stairs. At the top, the house guard did what the house guard always does: "By the order of the Lady of the House, you can't go in."

Hjumpik: "What if she's a fake?"

Waluigi wants that framed, mounted, and hung somewhere with good light. He said it as a DELAYING TACTIC. He had no idea. He was buying four seconds at a door and he accidentally described the entire situation, and within the hour he would be standing in front of the proof of it. This archive has filed a great deal of accidental prophecy and that is the cheapest and the best of it.

"I don't have time. If you close the door, bring us in — we can talk."

"Fine. Fine." The guards stood down. Everybody ran in. The Legion arrived behind them and started BANGING.

And then Hjumpik looked around the room and stopped, because the room was the room where he and Waluigi used the freezing spell, and the frozen statues were gone, and the engagement the party left IN PROGRESS was gone, and there was NOTHING IN IT.

So he asked the guards what had happened recently, and got this: "Well, we were at the hot spa, and we planned a push. So we killed some tree monsters and cut some leaves. But by the time we reached this room, we found some frozen statues in here and no plants to be seen. Soon the Lady returned. She asked us to guard the room while she does some preparation to kill the plants. So we have been doing that."

"No one else came in or out?"

"We're guards."

"Sure."

And then Hjumpik did the arithmetic out loud.

Three months in this house. He said it. He kept talking. And the number MOVED.

*Five months.*

He looked at his cowbell. He recalled his past. He RELEARNED it — that is the only verb available and Waluigi is using it under protest. Waluigi waved a hand in front of the dwarf's face and got NOTHING. No reaction. Not a flicker. The party's strategist standing in a guarded room with the Mages' Guild beating on a door downstairs and two entire months arriving in his head at once.

Waluigi is going to hold three facts next to each other and NOT resolve them, because resolving them is next session's job:

One. The Lady asked these guards to hold this room while she *prepares to kill the plants* — and the Lady is a plant.

Two. Nobody has come in or out. Because they are GUARDS. That is the whole of their reasoning and they offered it as though it settled something.

Three. Hjumpik has lost two months that he did not know he had lost, in a house where time is already suspect, with a cowbell in his hand that has now done something inexplicable in TWO CONSECUTIVE FILINGS.

That is not a character note. Waluigi is not filing it as colour. That is a SECURITY PROBLEM and Waluigi has put it in the investigation file whether the dwarf likes it or not.

sections.heading: They Read Him The REGULATIONS. In A Corridor. During A SIEGE.
sections.body:
The stair doors burst open and the Colour Division came through, and THIS one was an actual ambush — planned, sprung, executed — which after everything in this session Waluigi finds almost restful.

They apprehended Toad Lee and Waluigi promptly and without any theatre at all, which Waluigi RESENTED and continues to resent.

Hjumpik: "You got me. I'm Hjumpik."

He thought about asking for more time. Then he decided against time and asked for something NARROWER, which is the most Hjumpik decision in this filing: "No, I don't want to get any time. Just let me investigate first."

"Well — YOU can. But your friends there are apprehended right now."

"Why don't you just want me? Why them, in the crossfire?"

**"Leverage."**

One word. Waluigi has been in three courts and Waluigi has never heard a position stated that economically.

And Waluigi will admit — Waluigi did not want to kill the Mages' Guild. The option was AVAILABLE. Waluigi considered it. The consideration was brief but it was REAL, and Waluigi is filing it because an archive that only records the decisions you are proud of is a pamphlet.

"You know what — fine. Sure. I'll see what's in this room."

"Wait. Please read this."

And they handed a dwarf — in a corridor, mid-siege, with trees eating the floor below him — SIX PAGES of the Autumnwood Accords. Three thousand seven hundred and twenty-six words on containment and isolation zone maintenance. Structural integrity. Environmental stability. Arcane sensors and environmental data loggers. Staff rotation under § 1.20 to prevent BURNOUT.

BURNOUT. There is a clause about STAFF BURNOUT being read aloud to a man holding a warhammer while a manor collapses.

Hjumpik, having actually read it, because he is the kind of dwarf who reads things: "You want me to monitor this place?"

"No. That's what *we* are tasked to do."

Which — Waluigi hopes the reader caught that, because Waluigi nearly did not — means the Guild has ALREADY CLASSIFIED this manor as a containment zone and never told the contractor it left inside it.

Then they read him the part that was actually about him. *In the event that a bound object flees its designated location, the Aegis Magi may be authorized to track and retrieve it using Recall magic, the costs of which shall be borne by the owner.* And then: **collateral that can walk away requires extraordinary security.**

Waluigi would like every reader to sit with the phrase *collateral that can walk away*. They did not send four operatives across a plane for a REPORT. In that document, the dwarf is not the Guild's contractor. He is its SECURITY.

"Your mission is over, Hjumpik. You failed."

"You said it was simple. Look what happened. Plants came. Other stuff. No flak."

"Well — what have you achieved? Something *tangible*?"

"I'm getting to the bottom of this place."

"Anything tangible to show the Aegis Magi, and maybe they'll hold off a bit."

And Hjumpik put his hand in his pocket and CLUTCHED THE RING. The soul ring. With Lady Aurelian in it. The one thing he has that would satisfy them, and the one thing he will never hand over, and he did not mention it.

"How about this. Since you've got me cornered — I'll just check the room over there. I'll come back out. Hold me back for a bit."

"We want something, then. Insurance. Give us one item."

"You have my friends. You're lucky I'm not blasting you guys."

"Fine. Go get the mage cages."

And Hjumpik had the warhammer in his hand without appearing to have picked it up. "No cages. They're not animals. Just hold them."

"Fine." Handcuffs instead.

He signalled Waluigi to escape if things went bad. Waluigi slipped the handcuffs IMMEDIATELY — they are cuffs, Waluigi is Waluigi — and then stood there wearing them anyway, because there is no theatre in an empty cuff and Waluigi had just negotiated an exchange rate on exactly this. WAH.

sections.heading: He Killed A Monster's Composure With A Question About FURNITURE
sections.body:
He opened the door gently. "Ready to go, Hjumpik," said the satyr, who had been there the whole time and who nobody has explained.

"Sure. Why not."

They took one step in. The doors closed. Vines LOCKED them.

*"Yes, yes — come in,"* said Aurelian. *"We need to talk."*

"Yeah.... sure."

Hjumpik walked forward. **"Come face me."** — and then, one step later, out loud, to the room, in the finest piece of delayed self-awareness this archive has ever recorded: "Wait — why did I come in here? Actually, this was a horrible idea."

The vines covered every door. The whole room was crawling. He kept walking.

"Who are you?"

"I'm the one that will rule the manor."

"You're collapsing this place."

"Yes. And once it collapses, trees will grow anew."

"Then why impersonate the lady?"

"I needed to move some puzzle pieces. Put them into place."

"Why not just — why waste our time? Go out and kill everyone."

"Well. The beauty of nature is *slow*." A pause. "Have you smelt the fungus spores yet?"

It ANSWERED EVERYTHING. Every question, in order, at length, without evasion. And the ONLY reason the party has that confession is that the thing had already sealed the doors and counted the room as WON, and a monster that has won can afford to be chatty.

And then Hjumpik looked at what it was SITTING ON.

"Since we're dying anyway — what plant are you sitting on?"

"Oh, this? Sadly, it's just a foflower."

"Is it?"

"Yes."

"Ever wondered if sitting on this is bad for plants?"

He took another step. "You sure?"

"Hmmm. What do you mean?"

He SMIRKED. "Are you sure that plant is good to sit on? Plants are *carnivorous*, right—"

**"That's.... my name....."**

Waluigi has transcribed the pauses because the PAUSES ARE THE EVIDENCE. A joke lands on the beat. This did not land — it TRAILED. Something inside that face heard a word and answered to it as though it had been ADDRESSED, and then a creature that had cheerfully explained its entire strategy declined to say one more syllable about it.

He got a NAME. Out of a fey. By being condescending about SEATING.

"I have something for you," Hjumpik said. "Since it's my last day — why don't I give you something special?"

He threw the food right at her. Red's dinner. The poison that withers the overgrowth in the hand, straight into the chest of the thing running it.

Waluigi has spent two entire filings demanding that this party be MORE THEATRICAL. The dwarf who HATES theatre just out-staged Waluigi with a bowl of kitchen slop and a question about furniture, and Waluigi is obliged by the standards of this archive to SAY SO IN PRINT. WAH.

sections.heading: The Show Can Begin, And Waluigi Does Not Know What Happened
sections.body:
It was DAMAGED. Damaged is not beaten, and the difference arrived immediately.

Its eyes started bleeding. Then the black came. Then the PLANTS came out of the eyes. The mouth went hollow and kept going, past the point where a mouth STOPS, and Hjumpik — who has stood inside a treant's reach twice in one night without changing expression — was HORRIFIED. Waluigi is recording that because he is not a man who is horrified on paper, and in three sessions Waluigi has never once had cause to write the word about him.

The floor OPENED.

*"The show can begin."*

The satyr ran at it — "I'll stop this" — and failed HORRIBLY. The plants on the floor SHRIEKED.

And Hjumpik rang the bell.

Aurelian glowed ORANGE and her eyes rolled back. The ring in his pocket GLOWED. And the satyr just... stood there.

Here is Waluigi dropping the voice for the second and last time, because the archive deserves it and because pretending otherwise would be a lie with a laugh track on it: **Waluigi does not know what happened.** Waluigi wants that written down, in Waluigi's own voice, in an archive Waluigi controls. A cowbell. An orange glow. A soul ring answering something. A monster caught halfway through becoming something else, and a satyr standing perfectly still in the middle of all of it.

Waluigi files what Waluigi can prove. That is the entire job. And what Waluigi can prove here is a sequence of events and not one single cause.

Then Hjumpik RAN — away from her, and directly into the violet fungus, because that is the kind of night it was. He jumped one. BARELY cleared it. Reached the locked bathroom door.

The bathroom was LOCKED.

So count the doors with Waluigi, one last time. The satyr is behind him, locked in a fight he did not pick. The Mages' Guild is in front of him, hammering. The floor is open in the room he just left, and something with ROOTS WHERE ITS EYES WERE is currently deciding what to grow into. And the dwarf who spent this entire session refusing to fight anything he could not read is standing between two shut doors with a cowbell in his hand.

Last filing ended in a doorway WALUIGI opened. This one ends at a door that will not open, with the same dwarf on the wrong side of it, and Waluigi one floor down in handcuffs Waluigi already escaped from and has not mentioned to anybody.

Somebody is eventually going to have to admit that this house has a PATTERN.

Waluigi said, in a corridor, that Waluigi cannot afford not to care any more. Waluigi has now seen the invoice. Waluigi is still going to pay it. WAH.

sections.heading: Forty-Four Turns Of A Faction Punching ITSELF In The Mouth
sections.body:
Waluigi has the combat ledger and Waluigi is going to read it HONESTLY, which means reading it against Waluigi's own side.

Three rounds. FORTY-FOUR NPC turns. Twenty-four attack actions. Thirteen spells. And the result was NO DECISION WHATSOEVER. Most of the fighting was a standstill. That is not Waluigi being bitter; that is the summary line on the log.

**Busiest combatant: the Satyr Swordfighter.** Eight multiattacks. And its focus was — the HOUSE GUARD. Not the treant. Not the mound. The manor's own soldiers. A fey swordsman spent the ENTIRE ENGAGEMENT attacking the people defending the building.

**Most-targeted: the Treant** — which sounds like progress for about half a second, until you count WHO was doing the targeting. The House Guard put six multiattacks into it with heavy crossbows, at reach 100 feet, which is a very confident way of achieving six points of damage. The Satyr Bard cast Sleep at it THREE TIMES. Sleep. At a TREE. The Satyr Sorcerer spent four spells on the SATYR SWORDFIGHTER — their own best blade. The Satyr Rogue emptied a hand crossbow and two shortswords into the SATYR BARD, took it from 26 to 15, and then Cunning Actioned away like a professional.

The Satyr Druid Thunderwaved the Swordfighter. The Sorcerer dropped a Colour Spray cone that caught the Treant AND the Druid. A Goblin Line Cook threw cutlery at the Swordfighter four times while eating packets of suspicious powder it calls *"seasoning"* — and Waluigi would like the record to note the Line Cook healed itself for ZERO every single time, which is the most honest thing in the whole document.

And the party? Nineteen points of damage, all of it from the HOUSE. Hjumpik took a crossbow bolt for seven, then another for ten. Toad Lee was shot at twice by the Veteran. A guard used Interception as a reaction to reduce a hit to zero, so the house was simultaneously shooting the party AND protecting the party, in the same engagement, with the same unit.

Meanwhile the Treant cast Animate Trees TWICE. Twice. It was not fighting a battle — it was REPRODUCING in the middle of one, and the only reason the treant count is not higher is that the room ran out of ROUNDS before the tree ran out of TREES.

And the sleeping one died. That is the last line in the log. Somebody went down ASLEEP, under an enchantment cast by their own side, and the log does not say who struck the last blow.

Waluigi's reading, and Waluigi will defend it: **this is not a battle report, it is a DIAGNOSIS.** The Revel is not a faction. It is a room full of individuals who have not agreed on an enemy. And morale was BOLD — in the EIGHTIES — for nearly every combatant, round after round. Frightened troops break and scatter. These did not break. They calmly, confidently, repeatedly attacked the same friendly target for three consecutive rounds.

Which leaves Waluigi with a possibility Waluigi does not enjoy: given what the party learned upstairs about WHO HAS BEEN WEARING THE LADY'S FACE, Waluigi is no longer confident that a fey attacking another fey in this house is a MISTAKE.

Waluigi will not assert control. No compulsion was observed, named, or saved against — Sleep, Colour Spray, Mockery and Thunderwave are all in the log and not one of them dominates anybody. A file that concludes mind control from a targeting table is guessing with arithmetic in front of it to look serious, and this archive has been embarrassed that way before.

So here is what the archive WILL say, and it is worse for planning purposes than a conspiracy: the Revel can no longer be counted as an ally. Not because it is treacherous. Because on three full rounds of evidence it CANNOT BE PREDICTED TO ATTACK THE ENEMY — and the fey spent two sessions planning an ambush around themselves. WAH.
